cases.name: one blob, one drop
cases.why: a chain runs through every mote missing the colour that was dropped, and a whole row of them is one drop

cases.name: a wall of the wrong colour
cases.why: cyan already holds blue, so the chain neither takes it nor crosses it - which is the whole of what makes colour a decision here

cases.name: two blobs the wash cannot cross between
cases.why: par counts drops, not bursts

cases.name: a burst under a stack
cases.why: gravity only pulls down, so a well collapses when a wash reaches something a drop never could - and the wash is read before the fall

cases.name: a pure mote finished by two bursts
cases.why: the red between a yellow blob and a magenta blob takes blue from one and green from the other, and bursts without anybody ever dropping on it - which is what a pure mote is for

cases.name: nothing on this board wants what the well deals
cases.why: proved unsolvable rather than timed out, which is the difference between a level that is broken and one that is too big

cases.name: a column with no room and a procession that opens badly
cases.why: the only mote yellow lacks is blue, so red and green both come to rest on the brim and the search will not count either - par is the fewest drops that empty a well without ever breaching the line

cases.name: a well that has to be emptied from the top down
cases.why: every drop lands on a column top, so what is buried is reached by the wash or not at all

cases.name: a shipped shape
cases.why: five rows, three regions and a scattering of pure motes - the shape a chapter actually authors

cases.name: one drop fills glass by one channel, however many bursts it sets off
cases.why: every wave of a drop carries that drop's colour, so a lens gains one channel per drop and no more - which is the whole of what makes a shot cost three drops and the chapter harder than its first cut

cases.name: glass filled the ordinary way fires sideways
cases.why: a well has gravity, so a lens rests on something: down is the thing holding it up and up is the sky. The cyan directly over the glass is untouched by the shot and has to be cooked afterwards, where the magenta two cells across is taken by it

cases.name: a beam is white, so it pops whatever it lands on
cases.why: glass holds all three by the time it goes off, so what it throws is all three. The magenta across the gap already holds the blue that was dropped - a wash would have been absorbed by it and a beam completes it - which is the whole of what separates a shot from a wash, and what three drops of charging buy

cases.name: a lens struck by another lens fires every way
cases.why: one drop takes the whole board: the burst fills the two-thirds pane, that fires sideways into the empty pane, and the empty pane was *struck* rather than filled, so it fires up and down as well and reaches the mote standing over it. That is the chain the chapter is built on, and it is the reason a lens knows how it was lit

cases.name: a drop is taken in by glass rather than stacking on it
cases.why: the valve that stops a well ever becoming unwinnable - a player who cleared every mote before feeding the lens was stranded, so a drop now feeds it at one channel a drop, while a burst beside it stays free

cases.name: empty glass costs three drops where two-thirds glass costs one
cases.why: the chapter's difficulty dial: measured, an empty lens leaves 7 boards in 90 solvable where two-thirds-full glass leaves 50

cases.name: glass falls into a gap like anything else
cases.why: a lens is a mote for gravity, the mote count, the brim and the fingerprint - it differs only in being charged rather than washed

cases.name: a whorl mixes the two motes beside it
cases.why: every other rule in this mode adds a *colour* to a cell - a drop adds one, a wash adds one, a beam adds three. This is the only place two *motes* are ever combined, so a yellow and a blue that were each a drop away from white are none

cases.name: a merge that does not reach white is still a merge
cases.why: two motes of the same colour draw together into one of that colour, which tidies the board and decides nothing - the distinction `fused` and `kindled` exist to keep apart, and the reason a board is authored against the second

cases.name: a whorl draws light and nothing else
cases.why: glass beside a whorl stays where it stands: pulling it in would mean deciding what a lens and a mote mix into, and two whorls tugging at each other is a rule nobody can read off a board

cases.name: a whorl with nothing beside it closes and is gone
cases.why: the valve, and the reason a well full of whorls is still winnable: a whorl that waited for a pair could never be got rid of, which is exactly the state the lens shipped with

cases.name: a mote two whorls both reach is let go by both
cases.why: the only symmetric answer available: giving it to one of them would be a reading order, in the one method this rule is arranged to keep free of one. Both whorls find that side empty and close

cases.name: a drop opens a whorl, whatever colour it is
cases.why: the same valve from the other side: a whorl is otherwise only reached by a chain, so without this a player who cleared every mote around one would be stranded on a board that could not be finished and would not end
